key_insight: A two-hidden-layer MLP with tailored ReLU-type activations can exactly encode piecewise polynomial finite element functions on simplicial meshes in any dimension.
engineering_relevance: This provides a constructive, training-free way to convert FEM solutions into neural-network form for surrogate modeling, compression, and hybrid simulation workflows.
method: First hidden layer uses ReLU^0 + ReLU to handle mesh-skeleton structure.
Second hidden layer uses degree-dependent ReLU^k to reproduce polynomial pieces exactly.
Supports zero-skeleton and prescribed-skeleton representations, including continuous FEM functions via half-open decomposition.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact representation results with parameter counts that scale linearly with the number of mesh elements and, in the continuous case, match the order of global degrees of freedom under shape-regular meshes.
watch_item: The construction is explicit but depends on detailed mesh and finite-element data, so practical implementation may be sensitive to mesh topology, polynomial degree, and parameter bookkeeping.
paper_title: Exact Representation of Piecewise Polynomial Finite Element Functions by Two-Hidden-Layer Multilayer Perceptrons
